sources.title: How we built our multi-agent research system
sources.number: Effort rules: simple fact-finding 1 agent with 3-10 tool calls; direct comparisons 2-4 subagents with 10-15 calls each; complex research more than 10 subagents. searched_not_found: A controlled, published experiment that holds the task fixed and compares a free-text summary handoff with a file or structured-record handoff on final-answer accuracy: not found. Closest are HiddenBench (structured exchange protocol), Facts Without Rules (summary vs typed fields) and the vendor artifact claim; the Routed Graph Handoff paper claims one but I saw only secondary coverage.

A direct measurement of how many errors a same-model checker agent misses when the errors come from the same model's own output inside a multi-agent workflow: not found. Evidence is indirect (correlated errors between models, self-preference, self-correction failure).
Per-system or per-task breakdown of MAST failure categories in the part of the paper I could read: not found in the text I received.
Replication by an independent group of the 'boundary gate beats end check' result (Hallucination Snowball): not found; it is one preprint on one linear financial pipeline.

Measurements of failures specific to a tree with one coordinator, per-field child sessions and short-lived helpers under each child: not found; all evidence is on chains, flat groups, debates or a single lead with parallel subagents.

False-positive rates of verifier agents inside multi-agent research systems: only scattered numbers in single preprints returned by search (a security sentinel study, a code-review study); not opened or verified, so not reported as findings.

No published study found that isolates hierarchy depth (orchestrator of orchestrators, more than two levels). Context-Folding is described as strictly two-level, and Cursor's planner-spawns-sub-planner design has no depth ablation.

No controlled study found that compares one long-context orchestrator against split fresh-context orchestrators on tokens and quality for research tasks; the closest evidence is vendor reports and the compaction papers above.
No equal-token-budget single-versus-team comparison on tool-using research agents found; the equal-budget papers (L2-03, L2-06) use matched reasoning tokens on reasoning or mixed benchmarks.
No measured study found of stall-detection thresholds beyond Magentic-One's threshold of 2 (no sweep reported) and Cursor's judge-and-restart cycle (no numbers).

The Context-Folding paper (https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.11967) reports an active context about 10 times smaller than ReAct baselines at matched or better performance, but I could not read per-benchmark numbers, so it is not a finding. The Anthropic context-management post (https://claude.com/blog/context-management) reports 39% (memory plus context editing) and 29% (context editing) gains and 84% fewer tokens on a 100-turn web search eval with Claude Sonnet 4.5; it is an internal vendor eval and I left it out of the list.
The 'Lost in Compaction' memory paper on a Hugging Face forum (recall 0 to 7% in the compacted zone) is a single unreviewed forum post that I did not open; not used.

A study that gives an agent a quiz on its own context (or on a knowledge pack) and shows the quiz score predicts the quality of the agent's next task. Searched for comprehension or context-use signals; found only related work (generating questions from a corpus and measuring accuracy with and without it, arXiv 2502.13691; a black-box predictor from follow-up queries, arXiv 2501.01558; a self-explain-then-quiz proxy) none of which I opened or which tests this claim directly.

A study measuring whether selected, checked knowledge in a reviewer's context improves its review of a piece of research work versus a cold review, beyond the reference-answer results in No Free Labels (an answer-checking task, not research review).

A measured test of the dual-model or quarantined-reader design on deep research or multi-step web research agents; CaMeL and AgentDojo are on tool-use tasks (email, banking, travel), TRAP and WASP on browsing sites.

A clean measurement of long context harming an LLM judge. Search snippets point to ContextualJudgeBench (faithfulness accuracy falls with context length), Judge-R1 and LongJudgeBench, but I did not open them and give no number.
A compute-matched comparison for the voting claim in 'More Agents Is All You Need': that paper states no equal-cost test (see notes).
Hidden-authorship test inside a multi-agent research pipeline (agents reading each other's anonymised output): found only the summarisation and QA judge studies above.

rows.why: Checking cards against their sources at entry is the right first gate: errors caught early survive far less (per-stage gates cut surviving errors from 58.4% to 16.2%, against an end-only check that barely helped). But the row promises that 'a checker reopens each card a conclusion rests on', and no step runs after the review, which is where the conclusions are written (lines 43-44 run in stage A; the review is stage B). The checker is also briefed by the child it checks, and its CHECK.json sits in that child's folder (lines 21, 113). The 95% sample gate fails a field because its checker was strict, even though the failed cards are already dropped.
rows.change: Replace the 95% sample gate with this rule: every card cited in pack.md's conclusions and in review.json must be confirmed. A script confirms that each link resolves and that each quote is on the page. The checker confirms the number and the conditions, and that the citing sentence stays within the card's conditions. Keep the sample's failure rate as a ledger measure, not as a gate. The checker's brief is a fixed file outside the child's folder, and CHECK.json goes in the checker's own folder.

rows.why: At review time the inputs are neutral (lines 63-65), which is sound. The leak comes earlier: each child writes its own question list 'from the direction file' (line 36), and that file states the owner's hopes (direction lines 5-7, 15, 22-35). Nobody checks whether a brief is neutral. Anchoring survived prompt fixes such as 'ignore the anchor' and reflection, and framing the brief as a question cut sycophancy more than an instruction did.
rows.change: Before wave 1, the coordinator writes all seven question lists in one file, as open questions with ids, with no overlap between fields and none of the owner's hopes. The owner approves the file at the first gate. Each child receives its own list and never sees the direction file. The problem sheet labels our sinks as 'one repository'.

rows.why: The first half holds: facts are not voted on, and a claim stands on a confirmed card. That matches the evidence that consensus is not verification. The second half does not hold. A second expert of the same model, with the same search tool and the same question list, shares the first one's correlated errors (when two models are both wrong they agree 42.3% of the time, and more within one provider), so their agreement means little. It also contradicts section 6, which says 'from the same pack' (lines 77-80), while amendment 1 step 4 says 'its own research' (lines 140-141).
rows.change: The second expert is a second fresh reviewer that reads the same frozen pack, from a different model family if one is available. A disagreement marks a claim weak; an agreement never raises one. The coordinator picks the fields that get a second expert after the first reviews are in, from the verdict table. Delete amendment 1 step 4, and delete 'so their agreement means something' from row 3.

rows.why: Hand-overs as files with fixed fields are supported by the evidence. A typed allowlist kept boundary metadata that free summaries dropped. Structured exchange recovered 0.800 against a summarising secretary's 0.241. Compressors lost the artifact trail. But the synthesis script exists nowhere: section 8 lists only a schema checker, and 'compared sentence by sentence' (line 79) cannot be scripted over free prose, because each expert picks its own approaches (line 66).
rows.change: The coordinator fixes a list of approach ids per field. review.json is keyed by approach id and measure. The script lists every key on which verdicts differ as 'experts disagree', with both reasons, the cards each side cited and each side's cheapest decisive test. A card's conditions and limits are copied field by field, never summarised. The schemas, the check script and the synthesis script are written and run on the pilot field's files before wave 1.

rows.why: Keeping web text with helpers and passing up a fixed form is the pattern the published defences measure best. 'An instruction found in a source is data' is a wish, though. On web agents, injection succeeded about one time in four on average, and prompt-level defences were bypassed by adaptive attacks. This review saw it happen: the recheck notes for L3-07 and L3-15 say the fetched page text ended with instructions aimed at the reader. The child also reads primary sources in the original itself (line 133), so source text does enter its window.
rows.change: Readers hold no write or shell tools. They return cards as their result, and the child writes the file. The schema rejects any text outside the card fields, and the quote is at most 15 words. The child reads originals only from must-read sources whose cards were confirmed.

rows.why: 'One writer per folder' is enforceable, but two shared files break it. Every session and agent writes research/LEDGER.jsonl (lines 100-101, 111), and every helper writes the source register (line 170). Both contradict line 90. Branches per child also imply one worktree per child, which the protocol does not state. Shared, concurrently edited artifacts are where agent teams failed: locking made 20 agents run at the throughput of 2-3, and pairs on a shared codebase had about 30% lower success.
rows.change: Each session writes its ledger lines in its own folder, and a script merges them. Each child runs in its own git worktree. Delete the source register (see row 7).

rows.why: The shared register is a writable shared file checked before every read. It contradicts rule 7.1, it races when two helpers check and then claim the same paper, and in separate worktrees it de-duplicates nothing across fields. It also stops a second expert, or a neighbouring field, from reading the paper central to its own question, which defeats the independence that row 3 relies on. Lock-like coordination was the measured throughput killer in the Cursor report.
rows.change: Delete the register. Field boundaries come from the coordinator-written question lists of row 2. Accept some overlap. After each wave, a script counts duplicate citation ids across the cards.jsonl files as a ledger measure, and the synthesis removes duplicates by citation id.

rows.why: Three levels, helpers that start nothing, and at most six helpers per child are structural bounds, and all three refuters agree they hold. Coordination overhead grows faster than the number of agents: turns are 7.2 for a single agent against 27.7 for a centralized team, with a fitted exponent of about 1.724. That supports keeping the caps. But 'a total cap' has no figure and no one who stops at it. It is also unclear whether the coordinator counts toward 'three sessions at once' (line 96 against line 188).
rows.change: Make the total cap the admission rule of row 14. State that the coordinator is the fourth process, or that waves hold two children.

rows.why: Every handler here lacks a runner. Nobody reads the heartbeat. 'Reported' (line 103) has no recipient. Usage is read only before and after a wave (line 97), so a wave can overrun. A coordinator that has ended its turn cannot act on a repair request, a stall or a cap. 'A late field is restarted' never says to stop the stalled session first. The one measured stall design, Magentic-One's progress ledger with a stall counter that forces a replan, was part of a bundle whose removal cost 31%. In MAST the most frequent failures were loops and not knowing when to stop.
rows.change: One background watcher script per wave. It polls the child folders and the session records, writes status.json (state, tokens, age of the last progress, any repair or done file), and exits on the first event: done, repair request, no new confirmed card or file within the time box, or usage over the field's allowance. Its exit wakes the coordinator. The coordinator stops a stalled session before it starts a replacement.

rows.why: Keeping state in files on disk is correct, and the practitioners report the same thing: the plan is saved because a long context gets truncated, and each cycle starts fresh from a written plan. But 'started again from its folder' restores an expert only if a frozen pack exists. Before that, it restores cards only. And four different paths back into a fresh session each have their own rules (lines 62, 72-73, 142-143, 173).
rows.change: Use one path. Any child that cannot go on, whether from a crash, the window or a repair, is replaced by a fresh session that reads the frozen pack and the must-read sections, and the ledger marks it 'from pack'. If no pack exists yet, the field restarts from its cards.jsonl. This becomes the normal review path of change 1.

rows.why: A small, focused coordinator context is well supported. Every model family scored higher on focused input (about 300 tokens) than on full input (about 113k). Information in the middle of a long input is used worse. Practitioners pass references to artifacts rather than contents. But the protocol gives the coordinator duties that need reading: writing the problem sheet from our measurement files (lines 30-31), judging whether 'the pack covers the field's questions' (line 53), and choosing adjudications. And its hand-over at 200,000 tokens is a self-written summary, the kind that drops constraints.
rows.change: The problem sheet becomes a leaf session of its own. Gate A's coverage test becomes a script: every question id is covered by at least one confirmed card. At a hand-over, the coordinator's state is status.json from the watcher, not a summary it writes itself.

rows.why: Nothing in the row bounds spend. The 300,000 ceiling is a window size, and a child keeps making calls at that size. By the protocol's own sizes (cards received, a pack of up to 90,000 tokens written in the window, five to eight originals, then the review inputs), the 'exception' is a likely path. The review, the most judgment-heavy step, then runs at the most crowded point of the window, where the long-context evidence says use is worst. Multi-agent research used about 15x the tokens of chat. No one measures the 'lean folder' claim.
rows.change: Do the review in a fresh session from the frozen pack (change 1), so the ceiling is no longer an exception path. Delete the 60,000 floor on the pack. Give each reader several sub-questions in one window. In the pilot, read one reader's first-call context from its transcript and record it.

rows.why: Under amendment 1 the knowledge check is a self-test. The child writes probe.json and its keys (lines 50-51) and then answers them with its own cards still in its window. The grader is the child's own helper. A pack that is wrong or lopsided passes, because the keys carry the same errors. The evidence says a self-written reference repeats the judge's own error: when the judge was wrong, its own reference gave 0.16 against 0.83 with a human reference. Self-correction with no outside signal does not improve. The pack check confirms transcription, not which sources were selected.
rows.change: Delete the self-written probe. The expert is certified by four checks a script or an outside checker can run. (1) Coverage: every question id in the coordinator-written list is covered by a confirmed card. (2) The reviewer's input manifest (pack hash, must-read list, fixed review files) matches its read calls. (3) Every card cited in the review is confirmed and used within its conditions. (4) A verdict that rests only on vendor or single-study cards is marked as judgment.

rows.why: Running one field end to end before committing the rest is the only place a budget can be grounded, and all refuters agree. But part C runs the measurement field before the pilot (lines 187-188 against line 177). Nothing turns the pilot's number into a stop. And the token counts it relies on are self-reported by models that cannot see them.
rows.change: Make the measurement field the pilot. Count tokens from the session transcripts by script. Write and test the schemas, the check script, the synthesis script and the watcher on its files. Afterwards a wave starts only if the remaining budget covers its fields at the pilot's measured cost per field, with a margin the owner sets.

new_risks.title: False negatives: a dismissed lead or a dropped field is never challenged
new_risks.why: The programme exists because one null result struck a family off the list (direction lines 4-7; line 43: 'Not found is not does not work'). Yet the only adversary attacks the strongest leads (line 82; row 2), and those will be tested by an experiment anyway. Verdicts of 'wrong form' or 'wrong problem' (line 68), and fields dropped at a gate (lines 94-95), are never re-examined, so a wrong dismissal is permanent.
new_risks.handling: Point the one existing refuter at every dismissal verdict on a family and at every dropped field, with the confirmed cards in hand. Strong leads go to the owner's test table.

new_risks.title: Selection bias: search ranking and vendor reports decide what the expert knows
new_risks.why: Readers find sources with one search tool, and the checker confirms the number, not whether the selection was fair. Gate A checks coverage, not balance. Input A shows the risk: a large share of what is citable on agent orchestration is vendor reports with no replication (Anthropic, Factory, Cursor, Cognition, Chroma). Deep research agents also invent more links the more they cite. The direction asks for vendor claims to be kept separate and for earlier research to be read first (direction lines 67-70), but no protocol rule applies either request.
new_risks.handling: Make the card's evidence field an enum (replicated, independent, single-study, vendor's own). The script marks any verdict that rests only on vendor or single-study cards as judgment. Add the earlier research files (direction line 70) to the coverage seed list, and the pack states which seeds it omits.

new_risks.title: A correct card applied outside its conditions
new_risks.why: The schema can check that a card id is present, but not that the card supports the sentence. Conditions and caveats are exactly what compression drops (marker survival fell while facts stayed at 0.97-1.00). Retrieval-grounded systems mostly err by citing passages that do not support the claim. The review form's 'every factual sentence cites a card' passes such a sentence.
new_risks.handling: In the post-review check of row 1, the checker judges whether each citing sentence stays within the card's conditions. The failure rate goes into the ledger, and a review above a rate the owner sets is returned once.

new_risks.title: The tree may not beat one session at the same budget
new_risks.why: At matched thinking-token budgets, a single agent was at least as accurate as every multi-agent layout on multi-hop questions (0.418 against 0.379-0.388 at 1k). Teams gained on decomposable work (+80.8%) and lost on sequential work (-50.3% to -70.0%), and the gains faded once a single agent was already good. No row asks whether the tree is worth it. Row 14 measures cost only, and part C's control has no score.
new_risks.handling: Run the control on the pilot field with the same budget and the same checks. Fix its score before it runs: share of confirmed citations, failures of condition fit, tokens and time. Record the result as one reading, not a verdict.

new_risks.title: A child that is busy but not progressing
new_risks.why: The most frequent labelled failures are loops, repeated steps, not knowing when to stop, and declaring completion without verification. A heartbeat shows only that a child is alive, not that it is making progress. Row 9 covers waiting on a stalled child, not one that spends while looping.
new_risks.handling: The watcher of row 9 measures progress as new confirmed cards or files, not liveness, and exits when there is none within the time box.

new_risks.title: The checker and the checked share blind spots where the check is a judgment
new_risks.why: Where the checker opens the source, it has an outside signal, and that kind of check works. But grading condition fit, and any prose judgment, is model judgment. Errors correlate within a provider, and judges favour text like their own even after labels are removed. Neither the protocol nor input A says which model the child is.
new_risks.handling: Ground every check in the quoted source passage. Where a judgment is unavoidable (condition fit, second reviewer), use a different model family if the account has one.

shape.balanced: Changes no decision. It restates 'three levels, never more' (line 15). No source tests whether equal depth matters. Drop it.
shape.keys_in_inner_nodes: This is a real decision, but it is row 11's decision, not a new one. The evidence supports it: focused context beats full context, information in the middle is used worse, and practitioners pass references to artifacts rather than contents (L2-12, L2-11, L1-11, L2-07). The protocol's own coordinator duties break it (problem sheet, gate A coverage, adjudication). Keep it as row 11 with the duties moved out. The label adds nothing.
shape.split_on_overflow: This is the one property that changes a decision, and it is the wrong change. It contradicts 'fixed before anything runs' (lines 12-13, 90). It fires at gate A, after the research budget is spent. And it cuts one expertise into two, so mechanisms that span the cut go unreviewed. No source supports splitting a field, and the scaling study shows hand-offs in sequential work lose. Replace it: cut an over-limit pack to its limit, list the rest under 'not covered', and add a new field only by an amendment on the owner's word.
shape.order_of_work: A real decision about sequence, but not a B+ tree property. As written it contradicts 'a pilot field first' (line 177 against lines 187-188). Fix: the measurement field is the pilot.
shape.single_session_control: The most valuable item in part C. Published work at matched budgets finds that a single agent often matches or beats teams on reasoning (L2-06, L3-02, L2-05), while teams win on decomposable breadth (L2-04, L2-02). So whether the tree earns its cost is a live question. As written it has no score, no equal checks and n=1. Fix the score beforehand, apply the same checker and gates, run it on the pilot field, and record the result as a reading.
shape.verdict: The tree as a plain hierarchy earns its place: a central coordinator that checks aggregation, leaves that never cross-talk, and disjoint outputs. In the evidence, a centralized check had the lowest trace-level error amplification (4.4 against 17.2 for independent agents), a hierarchy lost least to faulty agents (-5.51 against -23.72 for a chain), and planner/worker hierarchies beat lock-coordinated peers. The B+ tree analogy does not earn its place. Two of its properties restate existing rules, one contradicts the fixed tree, and the useful item (order of work) is not a B+ property. Delete the B+ bullets, keep 'order of work' and the scored control as plain rules.

map.owners_requirement:
What the sources support. A focused context beats a long, mixed one: every model scored higher on focused (about 300 tokens) than full (about 113k) input, one distractor lowered scores, and information in the middle is used worse (L2-12, L2-11, L3-12). A reviewer given a verified reference grades far better than a cold read: with a human reference the judge reached 0.83 on items it had itself got wrong, against 0.30 without one (L3-11). Fresh-context reviewers avoid the writer's context rot (L2-10). Checks work when they use something outside the draft, such as the source, tool output or another model, and fail when the model re-reads its own work (L1-12). So 'expert first' is right if the expertise is checked against sources and held in a focused window.

What the sources say against, or as limits. Knowledge packed by the same model carries that model's errors: a self-written reference repeated the judge's mistakes (0.16 when the judge was wrong), errors correlate within a provider, and self-preference persists after labels are removed (L3-11, L1-14, L3-09). Filling the window has diminishing or negative returns past a point (L2-11, L3-12). Packing knowledge compresses away caveats and the artifact trail unless they are typed fields (L1-08, L1-09, L2-15). A summarising middle step recovered far less than full disclosure (L1-07: 0.241 against 0.926). Anchoring and sycophancy survive prompt fixes and need neutral, question-form briefs (L3-07, L3-08). An expert's knowledge is also only as fair as the sources its search surfaced.

What the design delivers. Source cards with number, baseline, conditions, limits and a quote. A checker that opens sources and drops cards that fail. A review form in which every factual sentence cites a card and judgment is marked. Our work given as files, without the coordinator's opinion. A fixed list of review inputs.

Where it fails. Amendment 1 has the child review in the same window that holds its research process, including cards the checker later dropped and a pack of up to 90,000 tokens written out, so 'filled precisely, nothing else' (line 11) is no longer testable. The knowledge check is a self-set exam with self-written keys. The question list is written from a file that states the owner's hopes. The checker confirms transcription, not selection. The review likely runs near the 300,000 ceiling.

The design delivers the requirement if the review is done by a fresh session that reads only the frozen, checked pack, the must-read originals and the fixed review files, as sections 4 and 5 originally said. A script then checks its input manifest, and its expertise is certified by coverage of a coordinator-written question list and by an outside check of every card it cites, not by a self-quiz. This reverses part of amendment 1, so it is the owner's call under rule 7.8.

changes_ranked.change: Every review is done by a fresh session from the frozen pack, the must-read sections and the fixed review files. This one path also covers the ceiling, a crash, a repair, the second expert and the methodologist's late review of test designs. It deletes amendment 1 steps 3 and 5 and the separate restart rules of lines 62, 73 and 173. It needs the owner's word.
changes_ranked.effect_on_measures: Quality and hallucinations: the reviewer holds only checked knowledge, so dropped cards and research noise stay out. Token cost: review calls run on a smaller window. Time and throughput: one rule replaces four.
changes_ranked.cost: One more session start per field, plus the risk that the pack loses caveats. Mitigate by copying card fields verbatim and by reading the originals. It reverses part of the owner's amendment 1.

changes_ranked.change: Delete the self-written probe and the 95% sample gate. Check every card cited in pack.md and in review.json: a script confirms that the link resolves and the quote is on the page, and the checker confirms the number, the conditions and that the sentence stays within them. The sample failure rate becomes a ledger measure. The checker's brief is fixed outside the child's folder, and it writes in its own folder.
changes_ranked.effect_on_measures: Hallucinations and quality: a check at the boundary that matters, using an outside signal. Token count: removes one grader window per field.
changes_ranked.cost: One checker pass after each review, sized by the number of cards cited.

changes_ranked.change: The coordinator never reads. Before wave 1 it writes all seven question lists (open questions with ids, no overlap, none of the owner's hopes) and the approach ids per field, and the owner approves them at the first gate. Children get their list, not the direction file. Gate A coverage becomes a script over question ids. The problem sheet becomes a leaf session that includes published cost breakdowns and labels our sinks as 'one repository'.
changes_ranked.effect_on_measures: Quality: less anchoring, and coverage is tested against a list the child did not write. Token count: the coordinator window stays small. Enables the synthesis script.
changes_ranked.cost: An up-front coordinator step and one leaf session for the problem sheet.

changes_ranked.change: Delete the shared source register (row 7, second half). Each session keeps its ledger in its own folder, merged by script. Token counts come from transcripts, not self-reports. One git worktree per child.
changes_ranked.effect_on_measures: Throughput: no check-then-claim races and no extra calls. Quality: second experts and neighbouring fields can read central papers. The seven measures become measurable.
changes_ranked.cost: Some sources are read twice; the overlap is counted by script.

changes_ranked.change: One watcher script per wave replaces the heartbeat, the PC-awake rule, 'reported' and the per-wave usage read. It writes status.json and exits on done, repair, no progress, or over-allowance, which wakes the coordinator. The coordinator stops a stalled session before replacing it and hands over by pointing to status.json.
changes_ranked.effect_on_measures: Time taken and throughput: no silent stall. Token cost: an overrun or a looping child is caught within a field, not after a wave.
changes_ranked.cost: One script to write and test on the pilot. Whether a background process can hold the PC awake still needs checking.

changes_ranked.change: Budget: delete the half/quarter split (section 9) and the per-pack and per-expert ceilings (line 96). Use one admission rule: a wave starts only if the remaining cap covers its fields at the pilot's measured cost per field. Read usage after every field. State whether the coordinator counts in the three-session limit.
changes_ranked.effect_on_measures: Token count and cost: the cap becomes enforceable. Removes two rules that can no longer be accounted.

changes_ranked.change: The measurement field is the pilot. The schemas, the check script, the synthesis script and the watcher are written and run on its files before wave 1. The single-session control runs on the same field with equal budget and checks, and with its score fixed beforehand (confirmed-citation share, condition-fit failures, tokens, time). It is recorded as a reading.
changes_ranked.effect_on_measures: All seven: the unknown cost is measured, and whether the tree beats one session is tested before scale.
changes_ranked.cost: One extra field run for the control.

changes_ranked.change: The second expert is a second fresh reviewer from the same frozen pack, from a different model family where available. Its fields are chosen after the first reviews, from the verdict table. A disagreement marks a claim weak; an agreement never raises one. Delete amendment 1 step 4 and the agreement clause of row 3.
changes_ranked.effect_on_measures: Token cost: a review instead of a whole field run, three times. Quality: an honest reading of what agreement means.
changes_ranked.cost: Loses independent research, which the sources say buys little within one model. This is the owner's call.

changes_ranked.change: Aim the one refuter at every dismissal verdict on a family ('wrong form', 'wrong problem') and at every dropped field, instead of at the three strongest leads.
changes_ranked.effect_on_measures: Quality: catches the false negative the programme was started to avoid. Neutral on tokens.
changes_ranked.cost: None: the same role with a different target. Strong leads lose a pre-test attack but are tested by the experiment itself.

changes_ranked.change: Delete the B+ bullets 'balanced', 'inner nodes hold keys' and 'split on overflow'. An over-limit pack is cut to its limit, with the rest listed under 'not covered', and a new field needs an amendment. Delete the 60,000 floor on the pack.
changes_ranked.effect_on_measures: Quality: no padding, and no mid-run split of one expertise. Fewer rules to run.

changes_ranked.change: Make the card's evidence field an enum (replicated, independent, single-study, vendor's own). The script marks any verdict that rests only on vendor or single-study cards as judgment. The earlier research files join the coverage seed list.
changes_ranked.effect_on_measures: Quality and hallucinations: the owner sees how strong each verdict really is.
changes_ranked.cost: A schema change and a seed list. Logging every search query (R3-04) is left out.

changes_ranked.change: Readers: several sub-questions each, no write or shell tools, cards returned as their result and written by the child, and the schema rejects text outside the card fields. The pilot records one reader's first-call context from its transcript.
changes_ranked.effect_on_measures: Token count and cost: fewer fixed prefixes. Hallucinations and safety: page text cannot steer a tool-holding step.
changes_ranked.cost: Each reader has a longer window. Whether the prefix is mostly tool schemas is not established.

rejected.why: The structural point is accepted under change 6: no figure on the per-pack ceiling, a split that can no longer be accounted, usage read per wave. But the estimates of tokens per field and per programme rest on start sizes, per-call growth and reader costs taken from files outside the inputs to this review. They cannot be checked here, so nothing rests on them.

'Write the pack and cards through a script, not inline' does not remove the tokens. The pack's map, mechanism grouping and disagreements must be generated by the model, so they enter its window however they are saved; only card dumps can be scripted. The finding is accepted, and change 1 solves it.
A margin with no basis in the sources or the protocol. The admission rule is kept, and its margin is left to the owner.

rejected.id: R3-01 (blind probe with questions outside the cards)
rejected.why: A checker that researches the field from sources to write questions the pack does not answer is a second partial research run per field. That is more machinery than the gap is worth. Omissions are caught more cheaply by coverage of a coordinator-written question list (change 3) and by the refuter aimed at dismissals (change 9). The self-test diagnosis itself is accepted.

It adds a ruling round the protocol rightly forbids: debate rounds added little over voting, and homogeneous debate lowered accuracy (L3-01, L3-03). The keyed conflict detector is accepted. Judgment conflicts go to the owner's table with each side's cheapest decisive test, which is how the owner already chooses tests (line 86).

rejected.id: R3-07 (two-pass review with hash-frozen verdicts and diffs)
rejected.why: Two passes, a hash freeze and a diff script are more machinery than the risk warrants, and verdicts on our approaches cannot be written without seeing them. Accepted from the same finding: labelling the sinks 'one repository', adding published breakdowns to the problem sheet, and the question lists being written by the coordinator.
It keeps a shared cross-field file in order to save a reader's work. Deleting the register (R1-06, R2-11) is simpler and keeps the fields independent.

rejected.id: R3-05 (agreement counts only if each side cites a card the other does not)
rejected.why: A scripted rule placed on top of a comparison that the sources say is weak anyway within one model (L1-14, L3-05). 'Agreement never raises a claim' is simpler and does the same job.
More ledger machinery than the risk warrants. The evidence enum and the seed list cover the selection risk.

The split of the agent prefix into tool schemas and the rest comes from files outside these inputs, and R1 judged the lean folder to hold. Only the measurement fix (read one reader's first-call context in the pilot) is kept.

for_the_judge: Fresh reviewer against the same-window reviewer: the sources split. Focus and fresh context favour a fresh session (L2-12, L2-11, L3-12, L2-10). Compression losses favour keeping the researcher's window (L1-07: secretary 0.241 against reveal-all 0.926; L1-08; L1-09; L2-15; L2-16, where re-fetching tripled while completion looked unchanged). I ranked the fresh reviewer first on the grounds that the pack is typed cards, not a free summary. Amendment 1 is the owner's own word, so this is his decision under rule 7.8.

The knowledge check: R2 would delete it, R3 would write it blind from sources, and R1 would have a checker write it from confirmed cards. I chose deletion plus scripted coverage and a post-review card check. Only R3's form tests what the pack leaves out, at the cost of a second partial research run.

The second expert: amendment 1 and row 3 want independent research, R2 and R1 want the frozen pack, and R3 offers dropping it for the refuter. The sources (L1-14, L3-04, L3-05, L3-06) weaken both forms equally within one model family. Whether another family is available decides how much any second expert is worth.

Error spread in a tree: L1-05 shows errors snowballing in a pipeline without gates, while L1-06 shows short refining chains damping natural errors. The sign depends on the setup, so the pilot should measure it rather than assume it.

The refuter's target: aiming it at dismissals (R3-03) rests on the programme's own origin, not on a source. Leaving strong leads unattacked before testing is a judgment that their experiment will catch them.
The lean folder: R1 says it holds and R2 says it targets the wrong part of the prefix. R2's figures come from outside these inputs, so I could not settle it.

R1-04 says a coordinator out of its turn cannot keep the PC awake. That is a claim about the harness, not something in the protocol text. The watcher fix stands either way, but whether a background process holds keep-awake needs checking on the pilot.

Anchoring by our own result files: their conclusions (for example a null in a report title) may anchor the reviewer (L3-07, L3-09). I rejected R3's two-pass fix as too much machinery and am unsure that labelling is enough.

The refuters' window arithmetic (R1-02, R2-02, R3-10) uses estimated per-paper and per-call sizes. The direction of the argument holds against the protocol's own sizes, but how often the ceiling binds is unmeasured.
not_established: Whether a tree of sessions beats one session at the same budget for literature research and review. The matched-budget evidence covers multi-hop QA and coding benchmarks (L2-06, L3-02, L2-05), and the research-system gain is an internal vendor evaluation without a matched-token baseline (L2-01).
The week's allowance in tokens and how cache reads count against it, so whether 10% of the week covers the plan at all.
Whether a fresh reviewer from a frozen pack loses more, through compressed caveats and re-fetching, than it gains from a focused window. No source compares the two for expert review.
Whether a model family other than the child's is available for checkers and second reviewers, and how much that would reduce shared blind spots in this setting.
Whether the 10-of-12 threshold or any knowledge-check threshold is calibrated against anything.
Whether search ranking and the predominance of vendor reports materially shift the verdicts.

Whether injected instructions in papers a child reads in the original can steer it. Injection was observed in pages fetched for this review, but the measured rates are for browsing agents (L3-15), not readers of papers.
Whether a background watcher can hold the PC awake and wake the coordinator reliably on this harness.
What share of the helpers' fixed prefix a lean folder actually removes.
